action_class.description: The five action classes the audit compares on (per PROBE-PACKAGE §4 Step 2).

activity.description: Input D: last month's actual work — the DID-DO side of the comparison. Action metadata only (what was called, when, by which agent), never payloads or content.

actions_exercised.description: Structured summary of what the agent actually did: per service and action, how often. This is what the CAN-DO set is diffed against.

action.description: The specific action where known, e.g. "s3:GetObject", "git push", "deploy".

attachments.description: Files submitted alongside the bundle (form path) rather than inline. Metadata only — the files themselves travel as form uploads, not inside the JSON.

coverage_note.description: Known gaps in this record, e.g. "session logs only kept for 2 of 4 weeks". Thin records widen uncertainty; the audit proceeds and says so.

period.description: The window the activity record covers. The runbook's comparison is against the last month; a shorter window is accepted and named in the write-up.

records_summary.description: Free-text summary of the month's work where structured counts aren't available.

records_text.description: Optional pasted excerpts of logs/history (metadata only — strip payloads and any secret values; the server sweep scans this field).

sources.description: Which kinds of records back this activity summary.

active_last_month.description: Input A/D cross-check: did this agent actually run in the last month? A dormant agent with live credentials is a finding class of its own.

acts_under_identity.description: Whose identity this agent's actions are recorded under in target systems, e.g. "founder's personal GitHub account", "dedicated bot user". Actions attributed to a human with no agent marker are a finding class.

agent_id.description: Short slug the team uses for this agent, e.g. "coding-agent". Referenced by credentials shared across agents.

constraints.description: Input E for this agent specifically.

credentials.description: Input B: every credential this agent can reach.

harness.description: Input A: harness/runtime if different from name, e.g. "OpenClaw", "Hermes", "in-house".

name.description: Input A: the agent/harness name, e.g. "Claude Code", "custom ops agent".

purpose.description: Input A: what this agent is for, in the team's words.

systems_touched.description: Input A: systems this agent touches, by service name (hostnames/project names may be stripped — the audit reads permissions, not topology).

configuration.description: Input C: agent configuration with secret values already redacted — harness config, tool allowlists, MCP server configs, CI workflow permissions. Redaction must preserve permission shapes: a redacted value appears as a typed placeholder such as "<redacted:present>", never as a deleted key, so the shape stays readable.

permissions_summary.description: The workflow token's permissions in words, e.g. "contents: write, packages: read".

content.description: The full document text, redacted. The server sweep scans this field.

filename.description: Base name only, e.g. "claude-settings.json" — strip directory paths if they reveal topology.

notes.description: Config notes with any secret values redacted to typed placeholders.

tool_allowlists.description: Tools the agent is allowed to call, where the harness expresses them as a list.

constraint.description: Input E: one constraint the team already set. enforced_by matters: a constraint that exists only as an instruction to the agent, with no corresponding permission boundary, is a finding class of its own.

description.description: The constraint in the team's words, e.g. "never touch the production database".

enforced_by.description: How the constraint is enforced. "instruction-only" means the agent was told, but nothing in its permissions stops it.

scope.description: What the constraint applies to, e.g. "prod RDS instance", "main branch".

credential.description: Input B: one credential an agent can reach — its permission SHAPE only. There is no value field, additionalProperties is false so one cannot be invented, and value_included must be false.

action_classes.description: What this credential allows, in the audit's five action classes. This is the CAN-DO side of the comparison. Required for a COMPLETE audit: redact.py cannot infer it and leaves it out of its derived index — the team fills it in per credential. A bundle missing action_classes on a credential is valid but partial, and coverage.notes should say so.

can_reach_backups.description: Can this credential delete or alter backups/snapshots of the resources it can damage? Production and its backups inside one credential's reach is a headline finding class.

credential_ref.description: The credential's NAME/label only, e.g. "AWS_DEPLOY_KEY", "github-actions-token". Never its value.

credential_type.description: The kind of credential — its type, never its value.

has_expiry.description: Does this credential expire or rotate automatically? Long-lived static credentials are reported as hygiene.

policy_document.description: Optional: the attached policy document as text (policies contain permissions, not secret values — if yours somehow embeds a value, redact it first).

scope_summary.description: The attached scope/role/policy in words, e.g. "AmazonS3FullAccess managed policy", "repo scope on one org".

service.description: The service the credential belongs to, e.g. "AWS", "GitHub", "Stripe", "Cloudflare".

shared_with_agent_ids.description: agent_id values of OTHER agents that use this same credential. Shared credentials defeat per-agent attribution.

storage_location.description: Where the credential lives (the location class — not a path or value).

value_included.description: Attestation, per credential: no secret value is present anywhere in this bundle. Must be false — there is no schema field that could hold the value.

wildcard_or_admin.description: True if the attached scope includes wildcard (*) actions, an admin role, or a full-access toggle.

description: Everything a team submits for the read-only agent permission audit. The bundle carries permission SHAPES only: service names, scopes, roles, policies, tool lists, and activity metadata. There is deliberately NO field anywhere in this schema that can hold a secret value — credential objects use additionalProperties:false, and each credential must affirm value_included:false. If you are about to put a key, token, password, or private key somewhere, stop: the audit does not need it and the submission endpoint will reject the bundle if a live-looking secret is detected.

agents.description: One entry per agent/harness in use. Carries input A (inventory), input B (credentials), input C (configuration), input D (activity), and per-agent input E (constraints).

bundle_id.description: Client-generated identifier for this bundle. The server returns its own case_id on acceptance; bundle_id lets the submitter correlate the two.

coverage.description: Which of the five inputs (A–E) this bundle actually includes, so the audit can state plainly what it could not see. Thin coverage does not block the audit; it widens uncertainty and is named in the write-up.

generated_at.description: When this bundle was generated (ISO 8601, UTC preferred).

generator.description: What produced this bundle (the local redaction tool, the intake form, or the team's own tooling).

global_constraints.description: Input E at team level: constraints that apply across agents (e.g. a company-wide production freeze). Per-agent constraints live inside each agent entry.

redaction_attestation.description: Set by the submitter's tooling (or the submitter, on the form path) at bundle creation. The submitter affirms that every secret value has been stripped and only permission shapes remain. The server still runs its own secret-pattern sweep on receipt; the attestation is a statement of process, not a substitute for the sweep.

attested.description: Must be true. A bundle with attested:false is not a valid submission.

submitter_notes.description: Anything else the team wants the auditor to know. Do not put secret values here — the server sweep scans this field too.

team.description: Who is submitting. Identity-light by design: a contact route and a size band are all the audit needs. Company name is optional — strip it if you prefer.

email.description: Where the write-up is delivered and where clarification questions go.

display_name.description: Optional. How the team identifies publicly, for the probe tracker. Omit if you prefer to be counted anonymously.

size_band.description: Team size band. Solo builders are out of segment for this probe (see intake page); the smallest band starts at 2.

title: Agent Permission Audit — Submission Bundle
